author: robustness_design
question: Does a frozen keyed-memory implementation retain correct latest-value semantics when unrelated edits, corrections, deletion and delay are varied independently?
hypothesis: A keyed memory that genuinely implements latest-value lookup will preserve present-value recall after unrelated edits and delays, replace corrected values, and return UNKNOWN after deletion; balanced aggregate accuracy alone will not establish this behavior.
competing_explanations: An apparent recall gain comes from a fixed last-write or query position rather than the requested key.
The memory preserves associations but returns stale values after correction or deletion.
An always-UNKNOWN strategy exploits the absent/deleted class mixture.
A robustness loss is caused by longer sequences rather than by unrelated-key mutation itself.
predictions: On a fixed 8-key, 4-value vocabulary, unrelated edits to nonqueried keys will change at most 5 percentage points of queried-key accuracy when sequence length and query position are matched.

For a history and its paired correction, the answer will change to the new value; for its paired deletion, the answer will change to UNKNOWN. Each lifecycle category must reach 90% rather than relying on the pooled score.
Replacing unrelated mutations with length-matched distractors will distinguish mutation sensitivity from sequence-length sensitivity.
Query-key permutation with correspondingly permuted visible histories will preserve correctness, while inconsistent key permutation will impair addressed recall.
controls: Freeze implementation, any training recipe, all thresholds and the full protocol before generating final cases. Use separate development and final history seeds, exact duplicate exclusion and no final-panel tuning.

Generate 480 held-out base histories per data seed, balanced across present read, corrected read, deleted query and never-written query. Split keys and values uniformly within every feasible category, randomize query positions, and expose only event inputs to the implementation.

Use the same base bindings for every paired variant: ordinary recall, unrelated edits, length-matched distractors, queried-key correction and queried-key deletion. Preserve the requested key's true lifecycle when applying unrelated mutations.
Cross delays of 0, 8 and 24 with unrelated mutation counts of 0, 2 and 4; match total history length between mutation and distractor arms within each delay cell.

Use an independently implemented exact keyed store solely as a correctness reference and scorer; keep target maps and expected answers outside model inputs. Report always-UNKNOWN as a diagnostic floor, not a primary architecture competitor.

Where learned-model comparison is made, include a trained Transformer and GRU with common data, training exposure and tuning allowance; report parameters and actual elapsed compute, and make no architecture ranking when training qualification fails.

Fix 300 optimizer updates and 60 seconds per learned fit, three initialization seeds and three separately generated final data seeds. If a fit is unqualified, timed out or fails, retain its failure and exclude it from architecture-superiority claims.
ablations: Clear carried memory before each query while preserving visible inputs to test whether the state supplies information.
Disable replacement-on-correction and retain earlier key-value associations to expose stale-answer sensitivity.
Disable deletion/tombstone handling to verify that the deleted-query panel detects stale retained values.
Apply a matched irrelevant-key permutation versus a query-key permutation, scoring invariance and addressing separately.
stopping_rule: Run the fixed 480-base-history factorial panel for each of the three final data seeds exactly once after implementation freeze. Stop each learned fit at the first of 300 optimizer updates or 60 seconds; do not early-stop on final results or replace failed seeds. Success requires a paired present/corrected value-query accuracy gain over reset of at least 0.10, minimum accuracy across all four lifecycle categories at least 0.90, and no more than 0.05 paired loss from ordinary recall to a matched unrelated-mutation arm in every seed. Report per-cell counts, accuracy, stale-answer rate, UNKNOWN coverage, paired differences and a history-cluster bootstrap interval; initialization seeds share cases and must not be treated as independent data replications.
limitations: This is a proposed synthetic CPU diagnostic and has no observed results or qualification status yet.
Familiar keys and values test lifecycle semantics, not lexical novelty, natural-language agent quality or hidden structure discovery.
An exact keyed store may satisfy this contract by construction; that proves the harness detects lifecycle errors, not that a neural architecture has learned the same operation.
Three data seeds and a small fixed training allowance are insufficient for a general model ranking or a broad distribution-shift certificate.

The complete factorial contains several stress contrasts. The prespecified value-query gain, worst-category guard and matched-mutation degradation rule govern the primary decision; other contrasts remain diagnostic.
next_discriminating_test: If recall survives length-matched unrelated edits but correction or deletion fails, compare explicit latest-write replacement with append-only association under identical frozen histories. If all categories pass, preregister interleaved multiquery histories with held-out operation order and new key counts; do not reuse this final panel for tuning.
